transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess I’ve just been kind of stressed lately. Since my sister and her baby moved back home, things at the house have felt a lot more tense, and I’ve been more on edge than I usually am.

It’s not like I’m falling apart or anything, I’m still getting to class and the shop, but I’ve been showing up already worn out. I’ve snapped over dumb little things at home, which I don’t feel great about. And I’ve missed a couple deadlines and had to back out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight. I figured maybe I should talk to someone before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
Have you found yourself worrying a lot more than usual, even about things that didn’t used to bother you?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but since my sister and her baby moved back home, I’ve just been more on edge than usual. Little stuff at the house gets to me faster, and then I feel bad because I’ll snap when I probably didn’t need to.

And it kind of carries over — I’ll show up to class or the shop already drained, like I’m starting the day behind. I’m still getting things done mostly, but I’ve missed a couple deadlines and even backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that your worrying feels harder to control than it used to, or that you can't seem to stop worrying even when there's nothing specific going on?

Um… I don’t think it’s like I can’t stop worrying all the time. I mean, I do get stuck on stuff more than I used to, but usually there’s something going on that sets it off, if that makes sense.

If I’m busy or out of the house, I can usually push it aside. It’s more like it comes back when things are quiet. I don’t know if that counts as hard to control, but it’s not constant or anything.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or have a lack of energy more often than not, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Yeah… I guess I have noticed that. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m exhausted all the time or anything, because I’m still getting to class and the shop, but I’ve been showing up already kind of drained.

It’s mostly since my sister and her baby moved back home. Things at home have been more tense, and I think being on edge there just wears me out. So even if I haven’t done that much yet, I can feel like I’m already behind, if that makes sense.
Have you found it harder to focus or keep your mind on things lately, like classwork or tasks at the shop?

Yeah… a little, I think. Not like I can’t do anything, but it’s been harder to keep things straight lately.

I’m still getting by with class and at the shop, but I’ve missed a couple deadlines, which isn’t really like me. And I was supposed to help with the theater set, but I ended up backing out because I just felt like I couldn’t keep track of everything. I don’t know if that sounds bad… I’m not trying to make excuses. It just feels like since things got more stressful at home, my head’s been kind of full already.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed lately, especially in situations where you wouldn’t usually react that way?

Yeah… I guess I have been a little more irritable. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m yelling at everyone or anything, but at home especially I’ve been snapping over small stuff more than I normally would.

It’s mostly since my sister and her baby moved back in. The house just feels more tense, and I’m kind of already on edge, so little things bother me faster. Then I feel bad after, because it’s not really how I want to be.
Have you noticed any physical changes, like feeling restless, being easily fatigued, or having trouble sleeping, even if it's just mild?

Yeah… I mean, mildly, I guess. I don’t want to overstate it, but I do feel more on edge at home since my sister and the baby moved back in, and I get worn out faster than usual.

Even if I haven’t done a ton, I’ll show up to class or the shop already kind of drained. I’m still managing, mostly, but it’s been enough that I’ve missed a couple deadlines and backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me if you find yourself worrying a lot more than usual, even when there isn't a clear reason for it?

Yeah… I think so, but it’s mostly tied to what’s been going on at home. Since my sister and her baby moved back in, I’ve just been more on edge than usual. Like I’ll be at the house and little things bother me faster, or I’ll start worrying I’m not keeping up with everything.

I’m still getting by, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But I’ve been showing up to class or the shop already kind of drained, and I missed a couple deadlines. I also backed out of helping with the theater set because I felt like I couldn’t keep everything straight. I don’t know if that counts as worrying “a lot,” but it’s definitely more than normal for me.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even a little more than usual?

Yeah… a little. I don’t think it’s like I’m miserable all the time or anything, but I have felt more down than usual since my sister and her baby moved back home.

I’m still getting by, but I’m just more on edge at the house, and then I show up to class or the shop already drained. I guess I haven’t been as into things either — I backed out of helping with the theater set, not because I didn’t care, just because I felt like I couldn’t keep everything straight. And I’ve missed a couple deadlines too, which isn’t really like me. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed that you feel anxious or worried even when there isn’t anything specific happening or that you can point to as a reason?

I’m not totally sure. I don’t think it just comes out of nowhere, if that makes sense. Usually I can trace it back to something going on, or at least something I’m thinking about.

Maybe there are moments where I’m just kind of tense and I don’t know exactly why, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound like I’m anxious all the time for no reason. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a number of different things, not just the situation at home?

A little, yeah, but I think most of it still kind of comes back to the home situation. Like, since my sister and her baby moved back in, I’ve just been more on edge in general.

It spills over, I guess — I’ll be at class or at the shop already drained, and then I start worrying I’m not keeping up or I’ll miss something. I did miss a couple deadlines, and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I couldn’t keep everything straight. I don’t know if that counts as “a number of different things,” but it’s not like it’s totally separate from what’s going on at home.
Have you felt anxious or worried most days, even if just mildly, for a period of several weeks or more?

Yeah… I’d say most days, but not like nonstop or anything. It’s been around maybe a month now, since my sister and her baby moved back into the house. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, but it’s been there pretty regularly, if that makes sense.

Have you noticed that these feelings of being down or losing interest in things have occurred even when things at home were relatively calm, or do they seem to only happen when there’s tension at home?

It seems mostly tied to the tension at home, honestly. Like when things are calmer, I can feel a little better, or at least not as weighed down.

But since my sister and the baby moved back in, even small stuff at the house can set me off more than it should, and then I’ll go to class or the shop already kind of drained. I’m still getting by, I think, but I have missed a couple deadlines and I backed out of helping with the theater set because I just couldn’t keep everything straight. So… I guess it’s not only in the exact moment there’s tension, but it feels like it comes from that situation, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things even before your sister and her baby moved back home, or has this mostly started since that happened?

I think it mostly started after they moved back in. Before that I was doing okay, really — not perfect, but pretty normal for me.

It was within a couple weeks of the house getting more crowded that I noticed I was feeling more down and not as into things. I don’t want to overstate it, but yeah, the timing seems pretty connected.
